newsitem.title: UK: London platinum fixes at lowest since Jan 1994.
newsitem.headline: London platinum fixes at lowest since Jan 1994.

text.p: Platinum fixed at the lowest level since January 28, 1994 on Tuesday, undermined by slack industrial demand and spillover selling from weak gold prices.
The rare white metal, used in the auto, jewellery and electronics industries, fixed at $381.50 an ounce, compared to $383.00 an ounce on Monday afternoon.
Analysts said prices would find some support around $380 an ounce, but further declines toward $360 were possible.
Key Japanese demand for platinum and its sister metal palladium have been weak in recent months, partly due to sluggishness in the semiconductor industry, analysts said.
Ample supplies from big platinum producer Russia have also helped to undercut prices.
Platinum and other precious metals have come under heavy selling pressure from disillusioned investors in recent weeks, with gold and silver trading at the lowest levels in over a year.
